draft.title: Landscapes, beauty and tourism
card: People value landscapes for different reasons. Many value them for their beauty. Some also value them for spiritual meaning.
Mount Fuji in Japan is an example. People admire its shape and it also has spiritual meaning for many people.
Beautiful landscapes often draw tourists. Tourists spend money on food, places to stay and tours, which can bring income and jobs to local people.
Many visitors can also put pressure on a place. Crowds can cause litter, damage to tracks and wear on the environment.
draft.remember: Valued landscapes can attract tourists, which brings money but can also bring pressure.

a.q: Why can a beautiful landscape bring money to a local area?
opts: Tourists who visit spend money in the area
The government must pay local people to live there
Landscapes sell their beauty to other countries
Local people are paid for each photo taken
a.why: Tourists pay for food, places to stay and tours, which brings income. The other options describe payments that do not happen because of beauty alone.

b.q: A coastal track in Tasmania becomes popular, and thousands of walkers now use it each month. Which problem is most likely?
opts: Walkers wear down the track and leave litter
The scenery becomes less beautiful to everyone
Local businesses lose all their income
The landscape loses its meaning for people
b.why: Many visitors can damage tracks and leave litter, which is pressure on the place. More walkers usually bring income to local businesses, so losing all income is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what many boots on one track do.

a.best: Tourists who visit spend money in the area

b.best: Walkers wear down the track and leave litter

problems.detail: The distractor 'The government must pay local people to live there' uses 'must', an absolute the card does not use. This makes the option easy to rule out without knowing the idea.

a.q: Tourists come to see a famous waterfall near a town. How can this bring money to the town?

a.clue: Think about what visitors buy while they are there.
